language_instruction: **Source language:** Classical (literary) Mongolian in the traditional Uighur-Mongol vertical script, printed from woodblocks (Beijing Kanjur, 1718–20). It is NOT Manchu. Columns run top to bottom and are read from LEFT to RIGHT. Transcribe in Mongolian script (Unicode U+1800 block), one source column per line, in reading order. The margin carries a Chinese section/volume/folio label. Report the primary language in the <language> tag.

<margin>Volume <term>Ja</term> <gloss>Seventh</gloss>, Miscellaneous <note>Sutras, original: "ja eldeb"</note>, Upper <note>Part</note>, Folio Two</margin>
<margin>Sutras of Various Categories, Volume Seven, Upper Part, Folio Two <note>original: "諸品經第七卷上二"; Chinese catalog marker for the Miscellaneous Sutras section of the Mongolian Kanjur</note></margin>
Subduer of Adversaries <note>original: "činadus-i daruγči"</note>, Illuminator with
the Jewel of <term>Dhāraṇī</term> <gloss>sacred mnemonic formula; Mongolian: darani</gloss>, Creator of
the Splendor of <term>Lakṣaṇa</term> <gloss>auspicious bodily marks of a Buddha; Mongolian: laγšan</gloss>, Radiant with Manifold
Ornaments, and
Radiant with All-Pervading Light,
Radiant as the Sun,
headed by <term>Manjušri</term> <gloss>Mañjuśrī, Gentle Glory, the bodhisattva of transcendent wisdom</gloss>,
together with <note>all those</note> <term>bodisaduva</term> <gloss>bodhisattvas, awakening beings</gloss> and <term>maqasaduva</term> <gloss>mahāsattvas, great spiritual beings</gloss>
in assembly. At that time,
the Victoriously Transcendent Buddha <note>original: "ilaju tegüs nögčigsen burqan", translating Tibetan "bcom ldan 'das" and Sanskrit "Bhagavān", the Blessed One</note>
sent forth in abundance from his own body a light
manifestly produced by <term>ridi</term> <gloss>miraculous power, from Sanskrit ṛddhi</gloss>;
and by that light
he illuminated this three-thousandfold
great thousandfold world-system <note>original: "γurban mingγan yeke mingγan yirtinčü-yin oron", translating Sanskrit "trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātu", a Buddhist cosmos of a billion worlds</note>,
making it perfect with the majesty
of light; and having done so, the Victoriously Transcendent
Buddha graciously smiled,
and proclaimed this inspired
utterance <note>original: "joriγ-un jarliγ", translating Tibetan "ched du brjod pa" and Sanskrit "udāna", a solemn, spontaneous pronouncement</note> as follows:

<summary>This folio from the Miscellaneous Sutras section of the Mongolian Kanjur concludes the opening assembly list of bodhisattvas, headed by Mañjuśrī. It then describes the Buddha emitting a miraculous light that illuminates the entire billion-world cosmos before smiling and delivering a solemn pronouncement.</summary>
